name: Adrak Lehsun ki Sabzi
ingredients: 5 large ginger (adrak) roots (approx. 300g), young and tender, peeled and sliced into thin matchsticks
2 whole heads of garlic (lehsun), cloves separated, peeled, and thinly sliced lengthwise
3 tablespoons mustard oil (sarson ka tel), for authentic pungency
1 large onion (pyaaz), finely diced (substituted with 1 tablespoon dried pomegranate seeds/anardana for a tangy twist in traditional versions)
2 medium tomatoes (tamatar), pureed (or 1 tablespoon dried mango powder/amchur for a tangy variant)
1-2 green chilies (hari mirch), slit (adjust to taste)
1 tablespoon jaggery (gur), grated (optional, for a sweet-savory balance)
2 tablespoons fresh coriander leaves (dhaniya patta), chopped for garnish
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed kadhai or pan until it reaches smoking point. Reduce heat and let it cool slightly to preserve the oil's pungency. 2. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida; they should sizzle immediately. 3. Add sliced ginger and garlic; sauté on medium-low heat for 5–7 minutes until they turn golden and fragrant, stirring frequently. 4. Add chopped onions (or anardana, if using), turmeric, and green chilies. Cook until onions turn translucent (about 2 minutes). 5. Stir in tomato puree (or amchur powder) and coriander powder. Cook until oil separates from the masala. 6. Season with salt, add jaggery (if using), and mix well. 7. Pour 1/2 cup water, cover, and simmer on low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the ginger and garlic become tender and the gravy thickens. 8. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with phulkas or steamed rice.
description: Earthy, pungent, and elemental—a rustic homage to the robust flavors of garlic and ginger that define the heart of Punjabi cuisine.
